title: Cheesy Mexi Bean and Potato Bake
subtitle: with Coriander and Crusty Bread
description: Craving a dinner that’s delightfully delish and easy to get on the table? We’re on a mission to make cooking more fun, extra yum and even simpler – this recipe, packed with quality fresh ingredients, is all that and more. Get cooking!

steps.text: Parboil potato: Peel the potato and cut into 2cm chunks. Put in a medium saucepan of cold salted water and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 6-8 mins until almost tender (the potato won't be fully cooked). Reserve 125ml (½ cup) cooking water, then drain.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Finely chop the coriander leaves, discarding the stems. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Coarsely grate the cheese. Drain and rinse the beans. Lightly grease a 1.25L (5 cup) baking dish (see Kitchen hack).
Start bake: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Add the garlic, potato, Tex-Mex seasoning and 2 tsp tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant.

Add vegetables: Add the beans, tomatoes, reserved cooking water and 2 tsp barbecue sauce to the potato mixture and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, covered, for 5 mins or until slightly thickened. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Stir in half the coriander, then transfer the mixture to the baking dish.

Bake and serve up: Thickly slice the bread, then put the slices on top of the potato mixture. Scatter over the cheese. Bake for 10 mins or until golden. Scatter the remaining coriander on top, then divide among bowls and enjoy!

Kitchen hack: If you have an ovenproof frypan, use it to cook the bake on the stovetop, then simply top with the bread and cheese and put it in the oven, instead of transferring the mixture to a baking dish.
